_purpose_notes: PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT CONFIG. Differences vs config.json: walk_forward.enabled=false (single train/val split on the full history), data.train_end_date pushed to the latest available bar (so the model sees every regime through ~yesterday), data.trade_*_date collapsed (no eval slice — out-of-sample evaluation already done via the walk-forward config), seeds.list=[42, 1337, 7] for the deployment ensemble. Re-validate the recipe periodically by re-running stages 1-3 with config.json (which preserves the walk-forward setup).

data._ticker_list_notes: 9 tickers (HYG removed). HYG was originally part of the universe but FinRL silently drops it during stage 1 because its inception date (2007-04-11) post-dates download_start_date (2007-04-01), so the first ~10 trading days have no HYG data and the alignment step in preprocess_data discards the ticker. All walk-forward OOS validation (the equity curves, Sharpe distribution, kill-switch tripwires in USAGE_LIVE_TRADING.md) was computed on these 9 tickers, so production deployment uses the same 9 to stay consistent with what was validated. To re-introduce HYG, bump download_start_date to 2007-05-01 (or later), re-run stage 1, re-run the FULL walk-forward (config.json + stages 1-3) to revalidate the recipe on 10 tickers, then retrain production.
data._train_end_date_notes: Bump to the most recent fully-closed trading day before retraining. Stage 1 will fail if Yahoo doesn't have a bar at this date (weekend / holiday). The trade_* dates are intentionally collapsed to the same value — single-split mode does not use data/trade_data.pkl, and predict_tomorrow.py pulls its own fresh quotes.

seeds._list_notes: CANDIDATE POOL for training. Stage 2 (02_train.py) processes every seed in this list, producing one model per seed. PPO training is initialisation-dependent: some seeds escape the near-uniform initial policy and learn meaningful allocations, others stay stuck (best validation Sharpe at step 2500 = uniform baseline). Train a larger pool than you need; ensemble_size below selects the best-converged subset at inference.
seeds._ensemble_size_notes: How many of the trained candidates to use at INFERENCE TIME (predict_tomorrow.py, inspect_ensemble.py). When set to N < len(seeds.list), the inference scripts rank the candidates by number of validation Sharpe improvements during training (more is better; ties broken by best Sharpe) and use only the top N. When unset, null, or >= len(seeds.list), all candidates participate. Typical values: 3 (default), 5, 7. Use filter_seeds.py to see the ranking explicitly. 02_train.py ALWAYS uses the full candidate pool regardless of this knob - changing ensemble_size never requires retraining.

walk_forward._notes: DISABLED in the production config. The walk-forward setup lives in config.json and is the validation harness — it produces OOS metrics across 7 windows that prove the recipe is robust. The production model is trained on the entire train_start_date -> train_end_date range with no held-out test (a single fresh train run uses all available history).

early_stopping._notes: With ~17 years of training data and val_fraction=0.1, the validation slice is the last ~1.7 years. Large enough for a stable Sharpe estimate, small enough that train_only still has ~15 years of regimes. Reduce to 0.05 if you want the model to see more recent data at the cost of a noisier ES signal.

risk_off._notes: Non-learned safety valve - identical to the walk-forward config. The threshold was validated across the 7 OOS windows in the walk-forward run; do not retune it for the production model without re-validating.

execution._rebalance_band_notes: Portfolio-level L1 threshold (sum of |target - current| across tickers). When predict_tomorrow.py receives --current-weights and the L1 drift is BELOW this band, the script outputs HOLD - no trades for the day, the model's signal is treated as a no-op. Above the band, the per-ticker filter (min_weight_delta) is applied to the target and the result is emitted as REBALANCE. Set to 0.0 to disable skip-day logic (always rebalance). With a 9-ticker portfolio, a band of 0.02 corresponds to needing on average a ~22 bp shift PER TICKER before a rebalance is triggered - in practice this skips ~40-60%% of daily rebalances on quiet days.
execution._min_weight_delta_notes: Per-ticker delta below which the freeze takes the CURRENT weight instead of the proposed target. Mirrors backtrader_config.json's execution.min_weight_delta exactly (same default, same semantics). On REBALANCE days, any ticker whose |target - current| < this is frozen at current_weight, then the result is renormalised to sum to 1. Set to 0.0 to disable the per-ticker filter (execute the model's exact target). Both knobs apply ONLY when --current-weights is passed; without it, the script falls back to emitting the unfiltered ensemble target.
